Pirates hitters in the Fall League
Easton Carmichael, C (
No. 8
):
Carmichael was a Cape Cod League All-Star in 2024, then parlayed a strong junior season at Oklahoma into being the third college backstop to be drafted, going in the third round in 2025. He turned in a very solid first full season, making it to Double-A and hitting a combined 20 homers with 92 RBIs and an OPS of .825 while playing solid all-around defense behind the dish.
Jhonny Severino, 3B/OF (
No. 28
):
The Pirates got Severino from the Brewers at the 2023 Trade Deadline for Carlos Santana, and after a decent organizational debut in which he reached full-season ball for the first time, Severino really struggled in 2025 back with Single-A Bradenton. He still needs to work on his approach (105/33 K/BB ratio in 2026), but he finished second in the organization with 31 homers, taking advantage of a hitting-friendly home park in High-A Greensboro (.565 SLG vs. .484 on the road).
Pirates pitchers in the Fall League
Brandon Cain
, RHP:
The nephew of former big league outfielder Lorenzo Cain, Brandon spent two years in community college and then one at Oklahoma, where he played sparingly. A former outfielder who has converted to the mound, he threw well enough in the Draft League in 2025 for the Pirates to take him in the 19th round that summer. The right-hander is still figuring things out on the mound, but features arm strength (fastball up to 97 mph) and a decent changeup (43 percent miss rate across two levels of A ball in 2026).
Bryan Mena
, RHP:
The Pirates nabbed Mena in the Minor League phase of last year’s Rule 5 Draft and he spent the year pitching for High-A Greensboro. The brother of D-backs right-hander Cristian Mena (
AZ No. 26
), Bryan has the chance to develop into a workhorse with a solid sinker (1.37 GO/AO in 2026) while still learning to round out his repertoire, and he did miss some bats with both a curve and slider.
Subscribe to the MLB Pipeline Newsletter
Zander Mueth
, RHP:
Mueth had a promising first full season of pro ball in 2024 after the Pirates went over slot to sign the Illinois prep standout for $1.8 million in the 2023 Draft. It’s been rough sledding since and he’s yet to get past Single-A Bradenton. He has size (6-foot-6) and electric raw stuff, but he gets hit too much and hasn’t thrown enough strikes. He’s pitching out of the bullpen this fall, with the Pirates hoping he can simply let his stuff play in shorter stints.
Cristhian Tortosa
, LHP:
Tortosa entered pro ball back in July 2015 when he signed with the Tigers for $30,000. He signed with the Phillies as a Minor League free agent in 2025, then with the Pirates this June after Philadelphia released him. Pittsburgh worked with the 6-foot-4 lefty to change his pitch shapes and that led to a strikeout rate of better than 30 percent, particularly missing bats with his low-80s slider. But he needs a lot of work on his command (7.1 BB/9).
Michael Walsh
, RHP:
A ninth-round pick out of Yale in 2022, Walsh had trouble staying healthy at the upper levels of the Pirates’ system in 2026. He’s a spin monster with a low-80s slider that elicited a 47 percent miss rate this past year, according to Synergy. The Pirates think he can use the Fall League to make up for some lost innings and get him ready for Triple-A in 2027, with a chance at carving out a big league career as a slider-heavy reliever.

title: Murf Gray rises through 3 levels in first Minors season with Pirates | This story was excerpted from Aiden Stepansky’s Pirates Beat newsletter. To read the full newsletter, click here. And subscribe to get it regularly in your inbox.
text:
Inside this Pirates prospect's 3-level rise in first pro season
September 22nd, 2026
Aiden Stepansky
This story was excerpted from Aiden Stepansky’s Pirates Beat newsletter. To read the full newsletter,
click here
. And
subscribe
to get it regularly in your inbox.
PITTSBURGH -- The Pirates knew
Murf Gray
’s abilities stretched beyond Single-A Bradenton. But to get his feet wet in affiliated baseball in 2026, Gray began the year at the bottom to work his way up.
Fast-forward six months, and Gray has skyrocketed through Pittsburgh’s system.
“It's gotten better from who he was in April to who he's finishing up as in September,” Pirates director of coaching and player development Michael Chernow told MLB.com. “He's a better player in September than he was in April, and that's because of the work that he put in, because of the aptitude that he has to understand the game feedback and what's important.”
Still just 22 years old, Gray finished his first professional season in Double-A Altoona. Across three levels, Gray batted .305 with a .969 OPS and 32 home runs while surging onto MLB Pipeline's Top 100 Prospects list (
No. 91 overall
, No. 4 in the Pirates' system).
As Gray enters the offseason, even he was shocked at his quick success.
“Honestly, it surprised me a lot. The first year of pro ball, I went in with an open mind, just being ready to learn and grow as a player,” Gray told MLB.com in the Altoona Curve home dugout. “But along with that, just being a sponge, learning new things, picking up on habits from different guys and just being able to talk about approach, ground ball work, footwork, like every little detail that goes into a long season.”
The Pirates
selected Gray
out of Fresno State in the 2025 MLB Draft knowing, inside and out, the hit tool he possessed. After his selection in Competitive Balance Round B, Gray didn’t appear in affiliated ball that year as he added to his frame.
Chernow believes the organization has seen a gradual climb beyond the
eye-popping numbers
. Gray has leaned on daily improvements at the plate and at third base throughout his career to make bigger strides.
He first realized in his freshman year of college that he could play baseball for a living. While playing for the Wareham Gatemen of the Cape Cod Baseball League in 2024, he picked up the mental side of his game through hitting coach Mike Mobbs. Mobbs taught him to be stubborn in his approach and find consistency.
“No TOB was a big thing, which is transfer of blame,” Gray said. “So if I get out, make an error, do something wrong, I'm not going to blame that on the game. I'm not going to blame that on anybody else. I'm going to take full accountability for myself, figure it out and move on and learn.”
COMPLETE PIRATES PROSPECT COVERAGE
Pirates Top 30 prospects
2026 prospect stats
Draft pick stats
Highlights
A key area in which Gray was forced to take accountability was his
chase rate
. Chernow said the development staff emphasized the “value of a walk” and added patience to open up other avenues for damage.
Gray’s walk rate increased from High-A Greensboro to Double-A, improving his on-base percentage despite a dip in batting average. Gray found more of a challenge with Altoona, as the opponents’ pitches became better and their locations were more pristine. He still attempts to be a hitter first, with the power following.
“The biggest transition is thinking ahead and playing a chess game,” Gray said. “Making sure that approach carries throughout not only your first at-bat but throughout all your at-bats, throughout the game, and the rest of the season.”
“You're seeing positive trends with swing decisions, and the most encouraging thing is that there's been no trade-off in contact quality as a result,” Chernow said. “He's still getting a swing off; he's still able to do damage, and that's certainly his calling card: his ability to change the game in one swing.”
Gray entered pro ball as a Gold Glove finalist in college, but his large frame (6-foot-3, 230 pounds) points to a possible move to first base in the future. He’s worked to stay at the hot corner -- a position, Chernow says, Gray could ultimately play at the Major League level. Chernow added that the focus entering the offseason will be to improve Gray’s horizontal range.
Get the latest from the Pirates
Have the latest news, ticket information, and more from the Pirates and MLB delivered right to your inbox.
“It's just going to be about making sure that that right-left range is in a good spot," Chernow said. "And when he continues to prove that it is, I don't see any reason why he can't play third base."
As proven through recent top picks like Paul Skenes and Konnor Griffin, the Pirates aren’t afraid to move prospects quickly through the farm system and to the big leagues if they’re ready.
Gray’s 2026 season fits the bill. And he’ll be more than happy when that day comes.
“It's going to mean the world, man,” Gray said. “All the hard work, all the late nights, all the early mornings, all the things I can give to everybody that believed in me. If I get that opportunity, I can't be more thankful.”

title: Wilber Dotel, Khristian Curtis and Antwone Kelly allow 12 runs to Cubs | CHICAGO -- As Hall of Fame manager Jim Leyland used to say, momentum is only as good as tomorrow’s starting pitcher. Looking for their fifth straight win, the Pirates relied on three rookie pitchers to piece the puzzle together.
text:
Pirates' rookie pitchers falter as margin for error shrinks in NL Wild Card race
September 12th, 2026
Aiden Stepansky
CHICAGO -- As Hall of Fame manager Jim Leyland used to say, momentum is only as good as tomorrow’s starting pitcher. Looking for their fifth straight win, the Pirates relied on three rookie pitchers to piece the puzzle together.
It’s safe to say the rookies looked like rookies. Friday was supposed to be Braxton Ashcraft’s start day before he hit the
15-day injured list with right arm discomfort
. Instead,
Wilber Dotel
,
Khristian Curtis
and
Antwone Kelly
combined to allow 12 runs in eight innings while striking out just two batters. The Pirates’ pitching woes led to a
12-2 loss
to the Cubs.
The loss also drops the Pirates to 5 1/2 games back in the
National League Wild Card race
after the Padres' win over the Giants on Friday night.
Playoff picture: Bracket, pennant races, tiebreakers and more
“Anytime you lose a guy like Braxton, it makes it tough, and especially with what he's meant to us throughout the season,” Pirates manager Don Kelly said. “Tough game today, but a learning experience for these guys to go through it -- the energy, the magnitude of the game, everything -- and something they're going to learn from.”
In Ashcraft’s place, Dotel opened a bullpen game and breezed through the first inning. In the second, he loaded the bases with no outs and Chicago put three runs across to take a two-run lead. The Cubs offense leads baseball in runs, OPS and home runs.
Taking down the veteran-filled lineup is no easy task. Especially for a group of inexperienced pitchers.
View this post on Instagram
“Tough day,” Dotel said through translator Stephen Morales. "Good team, good lineup. A rough day for the whole team today, but all we can do is just go out there and be competitive and do our best.”
On the other side, Shota Imanaga is the Pirates' kryptonite. The Cubs' left-hander entered the game with a 3-0 career record and an ERA of 0.24 with 36 strikeouts in six starts against Pittsburgh. But rookie Konnor Griffin was unfazed.
The 20-year-old hammered a triple to right-center field, and scored one pitch later on Oneil Cruz’s single to take an early 1-0 lead. While one run would’ve been enough in three of the Pirates' last six games, they needed to put plenty more runs on the board at Wrigley to come close to a victory. Mixed with a Bryan Reynolds solo shot in the sixth, that was all the Pirates mustered offensively.
When Curtis entered for the bulk role starting in the third, he didn’t have too much success either. Michael Busch drove in Seiya Suzuki on a double into the right-center gap and Nico Hoerner scored Busch on a fielder’s choice.
The Pirates' plans unraveled in the bottom of the fourth. Already leading by four, the Cubs unleashed for four more runs, including a two-run homer by Alex Bregman. Curtis had pitched 11 innings with just two runs allowed to open his career. Against Chicago, he allowed six runs in three innings as Pittsburgh fell behind 9-1. He finished his outing with a seven-pitch, 1-2-3 fifth inning, saying he felt he was capable of producing like that in the first two frames.
“Sped myself up. Wasn't myself out there today,” Curtis said. “I just got to get better, get ready for next week, next outing I get, and just take that opportunity and do what I know I can do with it.”
Antwone Kelly entered and, like his predecessors, was beat around by the experienced Cubs.
Kelly gave up three straight hits to start the frame and two runs scored, pushing the lead to nine. A Pete Crow-Armstrong RBI single in the seventh ballooned Chicago’s advantage to 10, and Kelly sat down the Cubs in the eighth with the damage very much done.
Surging through the first leg of the Chicago road trip and needing every win they can get to keep their postseason dreams alive, the Pirates surely didn’t want to use a combination of three rookies on the mound. But after losing its All-Star in Ashcraft, Pittsburgh went with what they had and dealt with the consequences.

“Tough day and a good learning experience coming into this environment in a big game,” Don Kelly said. “It's easy to talk about the mindset of going 1-0 when you're winning. After a tough loss, we got to take the same mindset going into tomorrow.”

Pirates prospects Tre Phelps, Chris Rembert adjust to professional baseball | PITTSBURGH -- Baseball can be quite the whirlwind. Take the last three months of Tre Phelps’ life, for example.
When Phelps returned from Omaha, Neb., after a College World Series run with Georgia, he had just a few days before heading to Arizona for the MLB Draft Combine. After the
text:
Pirates prospects Phelps, Rembert adjust to first taste of pro ball
September 7th, 2026
Aiden Stepansky
Tre Phelps (left) and Chris Rembert are adjusting to a new routine after making the jump from college to pro ball.
PITTSBURGH -- Baseball can be quite the whirlwind. Take the last three months of
Tre Phelps
’ life, for example.
When Phelps returned from Omaha, Neb., after a College World Series run with Georgia, he had just a few days before heading to Arizona for the MLB Draft Combine. After the Combine, Phelps returned to Georgia until the MLB Draft just two weeks later. After the Pirates selected him in the ninth round, Phelps flew to Pittsburgh a few days later to sign his contract and then moved to Florida to start his career.
Before he knew it, Phelps was competing against professional pitching.
“That was kind of our first time seeing live pitching in a minute,” Phelps said.
Phelps and 51st overall selection
Chris Rembert
are the first Pirates 2026 Draft picks to jump into affiliated ball. Rembert, a second baseman out of Auburn, batted .284 with four doubles and four RBIs through his first 18 games with Single-A Bradenton, while Phelps, a third baseman from Georgia, hit .175 with one double, one home run and six RBIs through his first 17 games with the Marauders.
Both have transitioned quickly from the roaring crowds of the Southeastern Conference to the much quieter fields of Single-A baseball. Rembert, the Pirates'
No. 9 prospect
per MLB Pipeline, said he doesn’t feel quite the same adrenaline rush as he did in his college days. Phelps, Pittsburgh's
No. 23 prospect
, added that the environment is similar to midweek games at Georgia.
“You're gonna have to prepare your own energy a lot of the days in [Single-A],” Phelps said. “Not every single day, of course, especially given where you are, but be able to come out and prepare with your own energy and create that own energy and just thrive off of that.”
Still, the game is mostly the same. Phelps pointed out that the pace of play is faster with a shorter pitch clock, though the arms they face are largely the same skill level, albeit with somewhat less consistent command.
“It's a little harder to hit, just because a lot of the guys don't have great command, and they're just kind of throwing the ball versus in college, you have a scouting report, and a lot of the guys do have command, and you can look in certain spots, and the ball will be there,” Rembert said. “I would say that's the biggest adjustment.”
Even with a short time away, any time without game action can be difficult for batters to adjust to. Rembert described the time away from playing as “miserable,” but he continued training. He didn’t participate in drills at the Combine, but he did meet with 22 teams for interviews. Phelps did the same, meeting with nine teams.
Rembert didn’t play in any games at Pirate City in Bradenton, Fla., and his first at-bats came with the Marauders. He felt things were a little sped up at first, but as the games continued, his timing and confidence returned. Rembert said his mental skills and instincts grew considerably during his two-year college career.
Get the latest from the Pirates
Have the latest news, ticket information, and more from the Pirates and MLB delivered right to your inbox.
For Rembert and Phelps, the organization has yet to point out sweeping changes necessary for their development. Rembert figures Pittsburgh will let him play and address any issues in the offseason after he gets a taste of game action. Phelps said that for now, he's focused on sharpening tools to add consistency. There are, of course, advantages to being a professional.
Preparation is quite different, utilizing more technology and focusing more on sleep and nutrition, with fewer distractions and more free time. Phelps said that as a professional, he should be overprepared for games if he uses his time wisely.
Both are settling into this new life.
“Haven't played a game for a while coming into it, but I'd say now that I'm getting more comfortable in the box and getting used to everybody, everything and the schedule,” Rembert said. “It's pretty similar to college. The travel-wise and the time of day are pretty similar, but it's awesome to be able to go out and play baseball every day and not have to do school.”

Braxton Ashcraft
Braxton Blake Ashcraft...Wife’s name is Cassidy...Is a 2018 graduate of Robinson (Texas) High School, where he was 11-1 with 103 strikeouts in 70.1 innings as a senior...Had 37 touchdowns among his 104 receptions and 2090 yards as a junior on Robinson’s football team in 2016...Was committed to pitch at Baylor (Texas) University...Was signed by Pirates scout Phil Huttmann.
2025
Began the season with Indianapolis, where he pitched 3.1 innings as the Opening Day starter on 3/28 at St. Paul...Earned his first win after allowing one run and striking out six batters in 5.0 innings on 4/9 at Louisville...Struck out 17 batters over 12.0 total innings in his final two starts with the Indians on 5/14 vs. Louisville and 5/21 at Toledo...Was recalled by Pittsburgh on 5/26 and made his Major League debut that night at Arizona, tossing 3.0 scoreless innings in relief of starter Andrew Heaney...Became the first Pirates reliever to toss at least 3.0 scoreless innings of relief in his big-league debut since Jim Nelson (3.0 IP) on 5/30/70 vs. San Francisco (Bubba Chandler went on to do that with 4.0 scoreless innings in his MLB debut on 8/22 vs. Colorado)...Tossed 2.0 scoreless innings in his PNC Park debut on 6/4 vs. Houston...Earned his first Major League win with 1.1 scoreless innings in relief of Paul Skenes on 6/8 vs. Philadelphia...Allowed his first run on 6/11 vs. Miami, snapping a streak of 7.1 straight scoreless innings to begin his career...Made his first Major League start on 6/23 at Milwaukee, allowing just one hit in 3.0 scoreless innings...Joined Babe Adams (8/18/1909- G1 vs. St. Louis) as the only Pirates rookie relievers in the Modern Era (since 1901) to earn a victory while tossing 3.0 perfect innings when he did that in the 3-1 win on 7/29 at San Francisco...Returned to the rotation on 8/9 vs. Cincinnati and stayed there until his relief appearance on 9/9 at Baltimore...Allowed three runs over 4.0 innings in his start on 9/15 vs. Chicago (NL), his first time in seven starts allowing more than one run...Joined Los Angeles’ Fernando Valenzuela in 1981 (seven starts) as the only Major League pitchers in the Modern Era to pitch at least 3.0 innings and allow one or zero runs in each of their first six big-league starts...Struck out six batters over 3.0 perfect innings of relief on 9/20 vs. the Athletics, making him one of three Pirates relievers in the Modern Era to accomplish that, joining Bob Patterson on 5/25/91 vs. Philadelphia and Chan Ho Park on 10/1/2010 at Florida...Made his final appearance of the season as a starter on 9/25 at Cincinnati, allowing a season-high eight hits in 4.1 innings while suffering a 2-1 loss...Went 3-2 with a 3.22 ERA (36.1 IP/13 ER) in 18 relief appearances and 1-2 with a 2.16 ERA (33.1 IP/8 ER) in eight starts...Was one of two Major League pitchers from 5/26 (debut date) through the end of the season to pitch at least 65.0 innings and allow three or fewer home runs (69.2 IP/3 HR), along with Milwaukee’s Aaron Ashby, who allowed three home runs in 65.2 innings of work.
2024
Went 3-2 with a 2.84 ERA (73.0ip/23er) and 77 strikeouts in 16 combined appearances (14 starts) between Altoona and Indianapolis...Earned the win in the inaugural Spring Training Breakout Game against the Orioles on 3/14...Began the season with Altoona...Started on 4/9 vs. Harrisburg in Altoona’s Home Opener and gave up four runs in 3.0 innings in a no-decision...Made his lone Double-A relief appearance on 4/14 vs. Harrisburg (2.0ip/2r)...Suffered a loss while tossing a 6.0-inning complete game on 5/2 at Harrisburg (Game 1); gave up six runs (four earned) while throwing 80 pitches...Pitched 5.0 scoreless innings while winning his first decision on 5/8 vs. Somerset...Pitched 7.0 scoreless innings and had 10 strikeouts on 5/14 at Akron, but had a no-decision in the walk-off loss...Tossed 14.0 consecutive scoreless innings from 5/2-19...Went 1-1 with a 1.95 ERA (32.1ip/9r/7er) in six starts during the month of May...Finished tied for first in the Eastern League in strikeouts (39), fifth in ERA, fourth in innings pitched (39.0) and fifth in WHIP (0.99) in the month of May...Struck out a career-high 12 batters and did not walk a batter in 7.0 innings while winning his second decision on 6/6 at Richmond (the most punchouts by a Curve pitcher since Tyler Glasnow in 2015)...Was promoted to Indianapolis on 6/11...Made his Triple-A debut on 6/13 at Jacksonville and gave up one run in 6.0 innings for the win... Pitched 4.1 scoreless innings in his second start on 6/19 vs. Iowa...Tossed 5.0 scoreless innings on 6/25 at Rochester, but received a no-decision...Was placed on the seven-day injured list on 6/28 (retro to 6/27)...Was reinstated on 7/6 and tossed 3.0 scoreless innings of relief that day vs. Louisville...Returned to the injured list on 7/12 with recurring symptoms of lateral forearm tightness (was reinstated on 8/30)...Returned to the I.L. on 8/31 and missed the remainder of the season.
2023
Went a combined 0-3 with a 2.39 ERA (52.2ip/14er), 63 strikeouts, 11 walks, .231 batting average against and 1.08 WHIP in 19 starts between Bradenton, Greensboro, and Altoona…Finished with the 14th-best strikeout-to-walk ratio (5.73) in all of Minor League Baseball out of the 1362 pitchers who threw at least 50.0 innings… Began a rehab assignment with Bradenton on 4/9…Struck out five batters in 3.0 scoreless innings in his season debut on 4/9 vs. Clearwater…Struck out six batters in 3.1 scoreless innings in his final rehab start with Bradenton on 4/15 at Lakeland…Was activated from the seven-day injured list to Greensboro’s roster on 4/21…Struck out six batters in 4.0 scoreless innings in his season debut with Greensboro on 4/21…Spent one week on the development list from 5/9- 16 to manage innings…Was transferred to Altoona’s roster on 6/20…Allowed one unearned run in 3.0 innings in his Double-A debut on 6/21 against Bowie…Tossed 3.0 scoreless innings in his last outing on 8/10 before being placed on the development list for the remainder of the season on 8/11… Was rated as Pittsburgh’s No. 10 prospect according to Baseball America (No. 12 by MLB Pipeline) at the time he was added to the 40-man roster in November.
2022
Missed the entire season after undergoing Tommy John surgery.
2021
Spent the entire season with Greensboro…Recorded a 1.65 ERA (16.1ip/3er) in his four starts during May, allowing all three runs on solo homers…Was placed on the 60-day injured list on 7/27 before undergoing Tommy John surgery while missing the remainder of the season.

Lake David Bachar
In August 2019, the Amarillo Sod Poodles hosted "Bachar Strong Night" as a show of encouragement for Lake's father, David, who was diagnosed with cancer in January 2018. The Sod Poodles took the field in a Padres throwback-themed jersey with #BacharStrong on the sleeve and the phrase "No One Fights Alone" on the back, a phrase that became a Bachar family rallying cry in David's fight against cancer. The Bachar Strong jerseys were auctioned off following the game, with the proceeds going toward the Bachar family's medical expenses. The Padres also donated various items, including signed bats from Eric Hosmer and Wil Myers, as well as a signed game-worn Padres jersey. Bachar Strong T-Shirts were also available in the Sod Poodles team store...Prior to his 2016 campaign with the University of Wisconsin-Whitewater, was ranked No. 100 on Baseball America's Top 100 Draft Prospects. Also tabbed as the No. 1 prospect in the Northwoods League on Baseball America's 2015 Summer College League Top Prospects Index...His 103 strikeouts led the UW-Whitewater pitching staff and the Wisconsin Intercollegiate Athletic Conference while finishing fifth in the nation. His strikeout-total tied for the third-most in a single season in school program history...Was a member of the UW-Whitewater football team, and played football and baseball at Wheaton North High School, where he was all-conference for baseball and football and all-area in baseball.
2025
In a career-high 53 appearances (one start), posted an 8-2 record and 3.93 ERA (31 ER/71 IP) with 30 walks and 75 strikeouts with a .213 opponent’s AVG (55x258) over two stints in the Majors...Made his first career Opening Day roster with Miami...His 73 strikeouts were tied for the most among all rookie relievers in MLB with CHW’s B. Eisert. Marked the fourth-most strikeouts for a Marlins’ rookie reliever in club history, behind 2016 Kyle Barraclough (113), 2013 AJ Ramos (86) and 1998 Vic Darensbourgh (74)...Led the Marlins’ bullpen and was tied for fourth among Major League relievers with eight wins...Among Miami relievers, his 73 strikeouts were the second-most, while he ranked third in the ‘pen in innings (69) and fourth in appearances (52)...Did not allow an earned run in 11-consecutive appearances from March 29-April 28 and held opposition to a .071 AVG (3x42) during the streak...Posted a 9.28 ERA (11 ER/10.2 IP) in nine games in May with eight walks and 14 strikeouts. Was optioned to Triple-A Jacksonville on May 24 and recalled by Miami on June 10...Did not allow a run in eight of his nine appearances from the time of his recall (June 10) until the All-Star Break (July 11), going 2-0 with a 0.50 ERA (1 ER/18 IP), 0.89 WHIP and .180 opponent’s AVG (11x61)...Allowed five walks and struck out 17 batters in this span...In 31 games after his recall, he went 6-2 with a 3.45 ERA (17 ER/44.1 IP), converting three of four save opportunities...Recorded first career save on July 5 vs. Milwaukee, retiring all three batters he faced in a perfect ninth inning...Made first career start as an opener on Sept. 1 at Washington, suffering the loss after allowing two runs on two hits in two innings pitched, in a 2-0 Marlins loss. Struck out two batters in the outing...Was one of nine different Marlins relievers to record a save and one of six to record at least three saves...Missed three games while on the Paternity List from July 25-28.
2024
In 10 relief appearances with Miami, went 0-1 with a 3.86 ERA (4 ER/9.1 IP) with four walks and 11 strikeouts. Held opponents to a .278 AVG and owned a 1.50 WHIP...Made his Major League debut with the Marlins on Sept. 8 vs. PHI, striking out all three batters he faced on 16 pitches (11 strikes)...Did not allow a hit in first four appearances; did not allow a run in first six appearances; allowed runs in only one of 10 appearances (four ER on 9/21 vs. ATL)...Recorded a team-leading five holds from Sept. 8 through the end of the season, which was T-third-most in MLB. His 10 appearances since MLB debut were T-second-most in NL/T-sixth in MLB...Started the season with Triple-A El Paso, his first career Triple-A action after spending the 2022-23 seasons at Double-A. Went 6-3 with a 3.89 ERA (31 ER/71.2 IP) in 46 appearances (one start) with 32 walks against 85 strikeouts...Made one appearance at Triple-A Jacksonville, allowing one run on three hits in 1.0 inning pitched. Was recalled by Miami on Sept. 7 and spent the remainder of the season with the Major League team.
2023
Worked in a career-high 42 games for Double-A San Antonio and posted a career-best 2.69 ERA (18 ER, 60.1 IP) and a 5-1 record for the Missions...All 42 appearances he made came out of the bullpen, making it his first season he had not made a single start ... prior to 2023, the most appearances he had made in a single season was 27 (done in both 2022 and 2018)...Led the Missions in holds (eight) and appearances (42), and among San Antonio pitchers who made at least 20 appearances, his 2.69 ERA ranked second best to just Kevin Kopps' 2.63 ERA in his 33 appearances...Logged five saves on the year after posting a career-high six saves in 2022 ... prior to his 11 saves between the two seasons, he had just three saves in his prior four combined Minor League seasons...In the first half of the season, had a 4.01 ERA (11 ER, 24.2 IP) ... in the season's second half, he had a 1.77 ERA (seven ER, 35.2 IP) with 37 strikeouts against 11 walks...After posting a 8.10 ERA in eight April appearances, he bounced back in May with a 0.96 ERA in eight appearances... in each of the remaining four months of the season, his ERA did not exceed 2.45. Left-handed batters hit .253 against the right-hander, while righties hit .222...When pitching with runners in scoring position, he forced opposing hitters to a .192 batting average (14-for-73) with just five extra-base hits allowed and a .291 opposing on base percentage...Declared free agency on Nov. 6, 2023, and signed back with San Diego on Jan. 11, 2024 as a Minor League free agent.
2019
Played the majority of his 2019 campaign with Amarillo (AA), setting career bests in wins (8), games started (20), innings pitched (132.2) and strikeouts (133) while giving up a career-high 127 hits and 60 BB...Struck out a career-high 9 in 3 of his 4 starts from July 4-21…his 32 combined SO in that span ranked 2nd in all of Double-A and T-5th in the entire minors...Earned Texas League Pitcher of the Week honors for the week ending on July 21 after tossing a career-hightying 7.2-shutout innings, earning the win vs. Northwest Arkansas…he first tossed 7.2-shutout innings on July 4 vs. Frisco...Made 10 straight starts from April 24-June 17, pitching to a 3-2 record with AMA going 6-4 in that time...Went 2-for-8 (.250) at the plate with 1 BB, 2 RBI and 2 runs scored...Finished the season among Texas League leaders in wins (8, T-2nd), strikeouts (126, 5th) and innings pitched (126.2, 6th)…earned TL Post-Season All-Star honors...Made 3 appearances (2 starts) in the Sod Poodles' TL Championship title run…struck out 12 across 9.2 IP...Tied for the AMA staff lead in wins and ranked 2nd in games started (19), innings pitched (126.2), hits allowed (121), runs allowed (62), earned runs allowed (56) and strikeouts (126).
2018
Played in his 1st full professional season, posting careerhighs in losses (9), ERA (4.68), games (27), saves (2), SVO (2), runs (67), earned runs (60), hit batters (8) and opponent batting average (.264)...Made 9 consecutive starts for San Antonio (AA) from July 15-Sept 1, tossing 5.0 innings-or-more in 6 of those outings...Made his 1st professional appearance at the plate while with SA, going 0-for-9 with 3 SO across 6 games...His 15 HR allowed led SA and ranked T-5th in the TL… his 7 losses and 9 wild pitches were the most among SA pitchers, while his 38 BB tied for the most among the SA pitching staff with Cal Quantrill and Logan Allen...Made 2 relief appearances in SA's postseason run, including one appearance in the TL Championship Series vs. Tulsa…tossed 6.0 innings combined with 1 R (ER), 1 hit (HR), 1 BB and 8 SO.
2017
Made 13 appearances (7 starts) between the AZL Padres and Fort Wayne (A), going 5-1 with a 3.38 ERA (19 ER, 50.2 IP)...Did not allow a run through his 1st 4 appearances while with AZL Padres 1 but went on to allow opponents to score at least 1 run in 8 of his last 9 games between AZL Padres 1, AZL 2 and FW...Assigned to FW on July 28 and made 6 consecutive starts for the TinCaps, tossing 5.0 innings-or-more in 5 of those starts and 6.0 innings-or-more in 3 of those starts...Earned Midwest League Pitcher of the Week honors for FW for the week ending on August 20, during which he earned the win in his start on August 17 after tossing 7.0-perfect-innings vs. South Bend…FW ended up falling one out shy of a perfect game. Made 1 start for FW in Game 2 of the MWL Championship Series vs. Quad Cities, suffering the loss after allowing 1 R (earned) on 4 hits and 4 BB in 3.1 IP with 2 SO.
2016
Began his professional campaign by splitting time between the AZL Padres 1 (R), Lake Elsinore (A) and Fort Wayne (A)...Posted a 1-0 record with a 1.83 ERA through his 1st 6 games (4 starts) before falling to 0-2 with a 7.00 ERA in 4 games (1 start) with the AZL Padres 1…made 5 consecutive starts from July 3-31, 2016...Made 5 relief appearances between Lake Elsinore (A) and FW to round out his 1st professional season, holding opponents scoreless in 4 of those outings with just 4 hits allowed.

Hunter Harkins Barco...Is a 2019 graduate of the Bolles (Fla.) School, where he was 5-0 with a 1.84 ERA & 67 strikeouts as a senior...Was named to The Florida Times-Union All-First Coast team...Attended the University of Florida (2020-22), where he went 17-5 with a 3.18 ERA (152.2 IP/54 ER) and 189 strikeouts during his 30 appearances (29 starts) there...Was named a 2020 freshman All-American by Collegiate...Baseball after posting a 1.40 ERA across his five outings...Was a member of the 2021 Southeastern Conference All-Newcomer team after going 10-3 in his 16 starts...Was also on the USA Baseball Collegiate national team...Was named the No. 1 pitcher in NCAA Division I by D1Baseball on 3/30/22...Had a 2.50 ERA (50.1 IP/14 ER) and 69 strikeouts over nine starts in the 2022 season...Was signed by Pirates scout Cam Murphy.
2025
Pitched in two spring games as a non-roster invitee...Began the season with Altoona, where he pitched 4.0 scoreless innings as the Opening Day starter on 4/4 vs. Chesapeake...Struck out five batters in 4.0 scoreless innings on 4/10 at Akron...Earned his first win after allowing just one hit and striking out six batters over 5.0 scoreless innings on 4/16 vs. Somerset...Was named the Eastern League’s Pitcher of the Week for the week of 4/21-27 after striking out 16 batters over 7.2 scoreless innings in his two starts (4/22 and 4/27 at Chesapeake)…Was also named the Eastern League’s Pitcher of the Month for April after striking out 30 batters and not allowing a run over his five starts (20.2 IP)...Pitched 5.0 scoreless innings in his final Double-A start on 5/3 vs. Akron and set the Curve franchise record (since 1999) with 25.2 straight scoreless innings...Was one of two pitchers in Minor League Baseball to not allow an earned run from 4/4- 5/3, along with the Athletics’ Donny Troconis (22.0 IP)...Was promoted to Indianapolis on 5/6...Made his Triple-A debut on 5/9 vs. Columbus, allowing one run over 4.1 innings...Left his start on 5/15 vs. Louisville after just 0.1 inning (23 pitches)…Was placed on the seven-day injured list on 5/18 (retro to 5/17) with a left shoulder strain...Was reinstated from the I.L. on 5/31 and returned to the mound that night vs. Nashville, striking out seven batters over 3.0 scoreless innings...Earned his first win with Indianapolis on 6/12 (G1) vs. St. Paul after allowing one run in 5.0 innings...Made 16 straight starts to begin his time with the Indians before allowing four runs over 2.2 innings in his first relief appearance on 8/24 at Syracuse (was his first outing out of the bullpen at any level since doing that with Greensboro on 6/22/24 vs. Hudson Valley)...Made two more outings in relief on 8/30 vs. Buffalo and 9/5 at Columbus, allowing one run over 4.2 total innings... Made his final Triple-A start on 9/11 vs. Iowa, giving up two hits and one walk in 3.0 scoreless innings...Made his final appearance with Indianapolis in relief on 9/17 at Gwinnett, allowing one run in 2.0 innings...Went a combined 4-1 with a 2.81 ERA (99.1 IP/31 ER), 116 strikeouts and a .196 batting average against (70-for-358) over his 27 appearances (23 starts) split between Altoona and Indianapolis...Was selected by Pittsburgh on 9/23 and made his Major League debut out of the bullpen that night at Cincinnati, earning the win after pitching a scoreless sixth inning in the Pirates’ 4-2 victory...Became one of only four Pittsburgh left-handed relief pitchers in the Modern Era (since 1901) to earn the win in his big-league debut, joining Bill Werle on 4/22/49 vs. Cincinnati, Joe Gibbon on 4/17/60 (G2) vs. Cincinnati and Frank Carpin on 5/25/65 vs. Chicago (became the first Pirates left-handed pitcher to do that since Paul Maholm accomplished it in his start on 8/30/2005 at Milwaukee)...Allowed just one hit over his 2.0 scoreless innings of relief in the season finale on 9/28 at Atlanta, striking out three batters (first Major League strikeout was Ronald Acuña Jr.).
2024
Went a combined 4-2 with a 3.27 ERA (66.0 IP/24 ER) and 83 strikeouts in 16 appearances (14 starts) between Greensboro and Altoona...Began the season with Greensboro, where he posted a 2.55 ERA (42.1 IP/12 ER) after his first 10 starts...Posted a 1.80 ERA (15 IP/3 ER) in his final four appearances (two starts)…Was named the South Atlantic League Pitcher-of-the-Week for the week of 6/24-30...Was promoted to Altoona on 7/19...Struck out five batters in three scoreless innings while making his Double-A debut on 7/21 at Somerset...Was placed on the 7-day injured list on 7/30 (retro 7/29) with a left leg injury and missed the remainder of the season.
2023
Made his professional debut in the Florida Complex League on 7/20 and struck out four of the seven batters he faced in 2.0 scoreless innings as a starter on 7/23 vs. FCL Twins...Pitched 3.0 scoreless frames in relief on 7/25...Was promoted to Bradenton on 8/3 and made his first start on 8/6 vs. Tampa (0.2ip/0r)…Lost back-to-back starts on 8/12 at Fort Myers (2.0ip/2r/1er) and 8/18 vs. Lakeland (0.1ip/3er)…Pitched 4.0 scoreless frames and struck out seven batters on 9/1 vs. Palm Beach (Game 1)…Went 0-2 with a 3.44 ERA (18.1ip/8r/7er) and 28 strikeouts in nine total games (eight starts) between the two teams.

Roy Reuben Chandler
Roy Reuben (Bubba) Chandler...Was ranked by Baseball America as the 20th-best player (21st by MLB Pipeline) in the 2021 draft...Is a 2021 graduate of North Oconee High School in Bogart, Ga., where he went 8-1 with a 1.25 ERA and 96 strikeouts in 44.2 innings while setting a school record in the playoffs with a 17-strikeout performance during his senior year; also hit .411 with 12 doubles, eight home runs, 35 RBI and 41 runs scored while playing shortstop...Struck out 16 batters in seven innings during an abbreviated 2020 season while also hitting .435...Was a Collegiate Baseball first-team All-American selection as a multi-position athlete in 2021...Was named a Georgia 4-A all-state first-team selection in baseball during his senior season...Was the 2021 Region 8-AAAA Player of the Year in baseball...Played quarterback for three seasons at North Oconee, where he passed for 1,842 yards and 18 touchdowns while also rushing 79 times for 548 yards and six touchdowns as a senior...Was rated by Perfect Game as the 13th-best player in the class of 2021, the third-best player in the state of Georgia and the fourth-best right-handed pitcher among the class of 2021 (No. 1 in the state of Georgia among right-handed pitchers for the class of 2021)...Was committed to play both football and baseball at Clemson University prior to signing with the Pirates...Was signed by Pirates scout Cam Murphy.
2025
Entered the season rated by Baseball America as the No. 7 prospect in all of baseball...Pitched in three spring games as a non-roster invitee...Struck out four batters while pitching 2.0 perfect innings as the starter in the Spring Breakout Game on 3/14 at Philadelphia...Began the season at Indianapolis, where he struck out 12 batters over 6.2 combined scoreless innings in his first two starts on 4/3 (G1) vs. Iowa and 4/8 at Louisville...Was named the International League’s Pitcher of the Month for April after posting a 1.33 ERA (20.1 IP/3 ER), 27 strikeouts, a .106 batting average against (7-for-66) and a 0.64 WHIP in five starts (became the first Indians pitcher to win a monthly award since Zach Duke in May 2005)...Struck out a season-high nine batters while allowing one run in 5.0 innings on 5/1 at Omaha...Had a 2.54 ERA (28.1 IP/8 ER) and 42 strikeouts in six May starts... Had an 8.53 ERA (12.2 IP/13BR/12 ER) in five June starts...Struck out 13 batters over 12.0 combined scoreless innings in starts on 7/4 vs. Louisville and 7/10 vs. Gwinnett...Went 1-4 with a 7.43 ERA (26.2 IP/22 ER) in his final six Triple-A starts...Led the International League in strikeouts and games started from 4/3 (season debut) through 8/16 (final start)...Was selected by Pittsburgh on 8/22 and made his Major League debut that night vs. Colorado, securing a save with 4.0 scoreless innings...Was rated by both MLB Pipeline (No. 7) and Baseball America (No. 15) as a top-15 prospect in baseball at the time of his promotion...Earned his first Major League win with 4.0 scoreless innings of relief on 8/27 at St. Louis...Became one of five Major League pitchers since saves became an official statistic in 1969 to earn both a win and a save in his first two outings, joining Rick Waits (1973 with Texas, 1975 with Cleveland), Boston’s Bob Stanley (1977), New York (NL)’s Mardie Cornejo (1978) and Baltimore’s Mickey Weston (1989)...Also became one of four Major League relievers in the Modern Era (since 1901) to begin his career with two outings of at least 4.0 scoreless innings, joining Boston (AL)’s Hugh Bedient (1912), St. Louis’ Von McDaniel (1957) and Detroit’s Eric King (1986)...Earned his second win with 4.0 innings of relief on 9/2 vs. Los Angeles (NL)...Became one of three Major League pitchers since 1969 to earn two wins and a save in his first three games, along with Minnesota’s Tom Johnson (1974) and Cincinnati’s Hector Carrasco (1994)... Was also one of two Pirates relievers since at least 1900 to pitch at least 4.0 innings in each of his first three outings, along with Carmen Hill in 1915 (the last Major League pitcher to do that was Kansas City’s Atlee Hammaker in 1981)...Made his first start on 9/7 vs. Milwaukee, allowing nine runs in 2.2 innings while losing a 10-2 decision...Allowed one run in 6.0 innings on 9/13 at Washington (had a perfect game through 5.0 innings before Dylan Crews led off the sixth inning with a single)...Struck out six batters and allowed just one hit and one hit by pitch in 5.0 scoreless innings in a 2-0 win on 9/20 vs. the Athletics (he and Braxton Ashcraft became the first pair of Pirates pitchers since at least 1901 to each have six strikeouts and zero walks in a game)...Made his final start of the season on 9/27 at Atlanta, striking out six batters and allowing one run over 5.2 innings in a 3-1 win...Became the first Pirates pitcher in the Modern Era (since 1901) to make three straight starts with one or zero runs allowed, zero walks issued and at least six strikeouts...Also joined Milwaukee’s Corbin Burnes (four) in 2021, Arizona’s Zac Gallen (three) in 2023 and Detroit’s Tarik Skubal (three) in 2025 as the only Major League pitchers in the Modern Era to make three straight starts with four or fewer hits allowed, one or zero runs allowed, zero walks issued and at least six strikeouts...Went 2-1 with a 5.12 ERA (19.1 IP/11 ER) in four starts and 2-0 with a 2.25 ERA (12.0 IP/3 ER) over his three relief appearances...Was recognized as the organization’s Bob Friend Pitcher of the Year during Young Bucs Awards Week.
2024
Entered the season ranked 59th among Baseball America’s top 100 prospects…Went 10-7 with a 3.08 ERA (119.2 IP/41 ER) and 148 strikeouts in 26 total games (23 starts) between Altoona and Indianapolis...Represented the Pirates organization at the All-Star Futures Game while also being tabbed as the organization’s Minor League player of the year by Baseball America...Was a non-roster invitee during Spring Training...Began season with Altoona and was the Opening Day starter on 4/5 vs. Akron (3.1 IP/2 ER - no-decision)…Tossed four hitless innings and struck out six batters on 4/13 vs. Harrisburg...Picked up his first win on 4/18 at Bowie (6 IP/2 ER)…Started and faced only seven batters on 5/17 at Akron; he walked five, throwing 10 of his 33 pitches for strikes, and recording two outs while being charged with five runs...Was placed on the 7-day injured list on 5/19 (retro to 5/18) with right forearm tightness...Was reinstated on 5/29 and suffered his fourth loss that night vs. Portland (4.0 IP/2 ER)…Gave up one unearned run in five innings and lost a 1-0 decision on 6/4 at Richmond...Allowed two unearned runs in three innings of relief and picked up the win on 6/9 at Richmond...Had 10 strikeouts while tossing seven scoreless innings on 6/21 at Bowie...Was named the Eastern League Pitcher-of-the-Week for the week of 6/17-23...Struck out a career-high 11 batters and allowed two runs in 6.2 IP while winning his fourth decision on 6/27 vs. Akron...Finished the month of June tied for the second-most strikeouts (35) in the Eastern League while recording a 2.49 ERA, which ranked seventh in the league...Had consecutive 10-strikeout games on 6/21 at Bowie and 6/27 vs Akron, which marked the third time in team history that a Curve pitcher struck out 10 or more batters in back-to-back outings (also Tyler Glasnow in 2015 and Roansy Contreras in 2021)…Pitched 7.2 scoreless innings while winning his fifth game on 7/3 at Harrisburg...Pitched two perfect innings in his start on 7/9 vs. Bowie...Represented the Pirates at the 25th annual MLB Futures Game in Arlington, Texas, on 7/13; finished off a 6-1 victory for the National League with a scoreless seventh inning...Gave up one run in seven innings while winning his sixth decision in his final Double-A start on 8/2 vs. Richmond...Made his Triple-A debut on 8/9 at Nashville and pitched seven scoreless innings for the win...Was named the International League’s Pitcher-of-the-Week for the week of 8/5-11...Tossed six scoreless innings and tied career high with 11 strikeouts in his second start on 8/16 vs. St. Paul (no-decision)…Gave up one hit and struck out 10 batters in six scoreless innings while winning his fourth game on 9/10 vs. Rochester (began the game with five perfect innings)…Made his final start on 9/17 at St. Paul and gave up two runs and struck out eight batters in 5.1 innings (no-decision).
2023
Worked exclusively as a pitcher after beginning his professional career as a two-way player… Ranked third among all Pirates Minor Leaguers in strikeouts (128) while going a combined 10-4 with a 4.54 ERA (111.0ip/56er) in 25 starts between High-A Greensboro and Double-A Altoona...Entered the season rated by Baseball America as the “Best Athlete” and as having the “Best Fastball” in Pittsburgh’s minor league system…Began the year with Greensboro…Ranked second in the South Atlantic League in wins (nine), tied for sixth in strikeouts (120) and fifth in batting average against (.265)…Recorded a 1.85 ERA in his final eight starts with Greensboro, which was the second-lowest ERA among all qualified pitchers at the High-A level between 7/18 and 9/2…Retired 13 straight batters to begin his Double-A career, allowing only a bloop single in his Double-A debut on 9/8 vs. Harrisburg…Was one of 13 pitchers to reach Double-A at age 20-or-younger.

Attended Oregon State, where he went 18-5 with a 2.28 ERA (42 ER/165.2 IP) and 176 strikeouts in 62 games (seven starts) over three seasons (2017-19)...Was named Third Team All-American as a junior in 2019 after going 8-2 with a 2.03 ERA (14 ER/62 IP) and 74 strikeouts in 14 games (seven starts)...Helped lead Oregon State to the 2018 College World Series title as a sophomore...Threw four IP of relief in the CWS opener vs. North Carolina, allowing one run…Earned the win on June 22 vs. Mississippi State, giving up one hit over a career-high 5.1 scoreless IP in relief…Threw five IP in Game 2 of the finals vs. Arkansas, allowing two runs on five hits with no walks and seven strikeouts to move the Beavers within a game of the title.
2025
Led the White Sox and tied for 11th in the American League (fourth among left-handers) with 72 appearances in his first full season in the Major Leagues…His eight losses in relief tied for the second-highest total in the Major Leagues...His 72 appearances are the ninth-most by a left-handed pitcher in White Sox single-season history and most since Matt Thornton (74) in 2015…Joined Matt Thornton, Wilbur Wood, Dámaso Marte, Zach Duke, Neal Cotts, Kelly Wunsch and Scott Radinsky as the only Sox lefties to make 70-plus appearances in a single season...Recorded a 3.68 ERA (15 ER/36.2 IP) with a .239/.327/.406 slash line at home, compared to a 5.18 mark (19 ER/33 IP) and .313/.363/.590 on the road...Made the White Sox Opening Day roster after being claimed off waivers from Tampa Bay on Feb. 7…Worked 1.0 scoreless IP with a career-high three strikeouts in his season debut on March 31 vs. Minnesota...Was optioned to Class AAA Charlotte on April 7, but was recalled on April 11 for the remainder of the season...Matched his career high with three strikeouts (second time) over a season-high two IP on April 17 vs. the Athletics…Earned his first career win on April 20 at Boston, tossing 1.2 scoreless IP...Earned his first career save on April 24 at Minnesota, retiring three of the four batters faced in the seventh inning of a rain-shortened, 3-0 victory...Made his first career start on April 27 at the Athletics, allowing one run on two hits over one IP...Served as the opener for the second time on May 13 at Cincinnati, pitching a 1-2-3 first…Recorded his first career hold the next night at the Reds despite giving up one run over 0.2 IP...Made four consecutive scoreless appearances from May 24-June 3 (5.2 IP), allowing no hits with seven strikeouts…Earned his second win on May 28 at the Mets, working 1.1 scoreless IP with two strikeouts...Recorded his second save on June 10 at Houston, tossing a 1-2-3 ninth inning to close a 4-2 White Sox win...Made his third start and final on July 2 at Los Angeles-NL…Allowed a solo home run to Will Smith in the first inning...Made seven consecutive appearances without allowing an earned run from July 26-Aug. 10, striking out 11 batters…Matched his career high with three strikeouts over 1.1 scoreless IP on July 26 vs. the Cubs and Aug. 6 at Seattle...Recorded a 2.19 ERA (four ER/12.1 IP) with a .200 (9-for-45) opponents' average over 12 games in August…Earned his third win on Aug. 24 vs. Minnesota (1.1 scoreless IP)...Posted holds on Sept. 19 vs. San Diego (0.1 scoreless IP) and Sept. 26 at Washington (1.0 scoreless IP)…Suffered the loss in his final outing on Sept. 27 at Washington (one ER/0.1 IP).
2024
Spent most of the season at Class AAA Buffalo, making 42 appearances (four starts) … also appeared in three games over six stints with Toronto...His contract was selected from Buffalo on 6/17 … made his MLB debut that night vs. Boston, throwing 2.0 scoreless IP … was optioned to Buffalo on 6/18...Was appointed as the 27th player for a doubleheader on 7/29 at Baltimore … threw 2.2 IP in the opener, allowing three runs on four hits...Also was with the Blue Jays on 7/14, 8/26 and 9/1-5 but did not pitch in any of the three stints...Was recalled for the final time on 9/29 and threw 2.0 scoreless IP with two strikeouts that day vs. Miami in the season finale … fanned Jesús Sánchez for his first career strikeout.
2023
Appeared at MLB Spring Training for the second straight year, playing in five games posting a 4.15 ERA (2 ER/4.1 IP) with a pair of walks and three strikeouts...Spent the 2023 campaign at Triple-A Buffalo, making 59 appearances (one start) going 4-3 with a 4.17 ERA (32 ER/69.0 IP), 25 walks, 76 strikeouts and two saves...Posted a 3.04 strikeout-to-walk ratio, with a 26.2% strikeout percentage compared to a 8.6% walk percentage (17.6% K-BB%).
2022
Spent the entire 2022 season pitching for Triple-A Buffalo, making five starts and 40 appearances out of the bullpen... Went 4-3 with a 3.41 ERA (23 ER/60.2 IP) and a 1.14 WHIP... Struck out 77 batters while walking only 15.
2021
In his first professional season in 2021, spent time at Single-A Dunedin, High-A Vancouver, and Double-A New Hampshire...Combined to appear in 32 games, pitching to a 3.55 ERA (25 ER/63.1 IP) with 82 strikeouts and 19 walks...Started the 2021 campaign with a couple of scoreless outings for the D-Jays before a promotion to the Canadians...Went 5-1 across 20 games with Vancouver before joining the Fisher Cats...Posted a 2.63 ERA over 10 contests for the Cats to close out his season.
2020
Did not pitch following the cancellation of the Minor League season due to the COVID-19 pandemic...Was recommended by Blue Jays scout Ryan Fox.

Thomas Hinson Harrington...Wife’s name is Lindsey...Is a 2020 graduate of Southern Lee (N.C.) High School, where he helped lead the team to three consecutive conference championships from 2017-19 (went 4-0 with a 0.32 ERA and 54 strikeouts over 43.2 innings in 2019)...Attended Campbell (N.C.) University (2021-22), where he was honored as the 2022 Big South Conference Pitcher of the Year after leading NCAA Division I with 12 wins...Was the second-highest pick in school and conference history, trailing teammate Zach Neto (No. 13 in 2022)...Was also recognized as the 2021 Big South Conference Freshman of the Year after recording a 3.45 ERA, the fifth-lowest mark in the conference (lowest among qualified freshman starters), over 16 outings (14 starts)...Was signed by Pirates scout Mike Bradford.
2025
Entered the season rated by Baseball America as the No. 74 prospect in all of baseball...Pitched in four spring games (two starts) as a non-roster invitee, including the Grapefruit League finale on 3/24 at Minnesota...Did not appear in a Minor League game before being selected by the Pirates on 4/1...Made his Major League debut as a starter that night at Tampa Bay, allowing six runs over 4.0 innings in a 7-0 loss...Made his next appearance as a reliever on 4/7 vs. St. Louis, striking out five batters over 4.0 innings while securing a save (the first 4.0-inning save by a Pittsburgh pitcher since Jason Christiansen on 7/17/98 at Montréal)...Was also the fifth Pirates pitcher to record a save of at least 4.0 innings or more for their first save since the stat became official in 1969, the first since Jim Winn (4.0 IP) on 9/19/84 at Chicago...Became the third Pirates rookie with a 4.0-inning save, along with Kent Tekulve (4.0 IP) on 9/22/75 vs. Philadelphia and Blas Minor (5.0 IP) on 6/19/93 vs. New York (Bubba Chandler went on to secure a 4.0-inning save in his Major League debut on 8/22 vs. Colorado)...Also became one of four Major League pitchers since 1969 to start in his big-league debut and earn a save in his second game, according to the Elias Sports Bureau, joining Montréal’s Kent Bottenfield in 1992, Washington’s A.J. Cole in 2015 and Los Angeles (NL)’s Tony Gonsolin in 2019...Was optioned to Indianapolis following Pittsburgh’s win on 4/9 vs. St. Louis...Struck out three batters in 2.0 scoreless innings in his lone relief appearance with the Indians on 4/13 at Louisville...Struck out a season-high 10 batters while allowing two runs over 6.0 innings in a 4-2 win on 6/14 vs. St. Paul...Went 3-0 with a 2.75 ERA (19.2 IP/7 R/6 ER) over his first four July starts...Was recalled by Pittsburgh on 8/1 and pitched in relief that night at Colorado, allowing six runs in 0.1 inning...Was optioned back to Indianapolis, where he remained for the rest of the season, after the Pirates’ 17-16 loss that night...Allowed nine runs across 4.2 innings in his two relief appearances and six runs in 4.0 innings in his lone start...Started for the Indians on 8/8 vs. Omaha before being placed on the seven-day injured list with a groin injury on 8/10 (retro to 8/9)...Was reinstated from the I.L. on 8/28 and pitched a perfect first inning while starting that night vs. Buffalo...Was placed on the seven-day I.L. with a right groin strain on 8/29 and missed the remainder of the season.
2024
Was a non-roster invitee during Spring Training (made one appearance and tossed a scoreless inning against the Orioles on 2/29 at Sarasota)…Began regular season on the injured list at Altoona with a rotator cuff strain...Began a rehab assignment with Bradenton on 5/7; struck out three batters and yielded one hit in three scoreless innings vs. St. Lucie...Ended rehab and was activated at Altoona on 5/12; tossed three hitless innings in his start that day vs. Somerset (Game 2)…Pitched four hitless innings on 5/18 at Akron...Posted a 2.70 ERA (16.2ip/5er), 17 strikeouts and just one walk in four starts with Altoona in May...Made his only relief appearance on 6/5 at Richmond and surrendered six runs (five earned) in five innings...Suffered his first loss on 6/11 vs. Erie; gave up six runs (one earned) in 5.0ip...Pitched five scoreless innings on 6/16 vs. Erie (no-decision)…Gave up three hits in seven scoreless innings and picked up his first win on 7/4 at Harrisburg...Surrendered one run and struck out a career-high tying 11 batters on 7ip while winning his second game on 7/10 vs. Bowie...Struck out 10 batters in his next start on 7/20 at Somerset (6.0ip/1er)…Pitched 5.2 scoreless innings in a no-decision on 7/26 at Erie...Went 2-0 with a 0.70 ERA (25.2ip/2er), 32 strikeouts and a .170 batting average against in four starts during the month of July and was named the Eastern League Pitcher-of-the-Month...Led all Double-A pitchers in ERA and strikeouts in July...Was promoted to Indianapolis and made his first Triple-A start on 8/4 vs. Toledo; gave up five runs in 5.2ip (no-decision)…Allowed two hits and tossed seven scoreless innings while winning his first Triple-A game on 8/17 vs. St. Paul...Was named International League Pitcher-of-the-Week for the week of 8/12-18...Gave up one run on two hits and struck out six batters in 6ip while winning his second game on 6/23 at Columbus...Went 3-1 with a 3.81 ERA (28.1ip/12er) in five starts in August...Won his fourth decision on 9/11 vs. Rochester (6.2ip/2er)…Made his final start on 9/18 at Paul and gave up two runs (one earned) in 5.0ip while winning his fifth straight game with Indy...Went 7-3 with a 2.61 ERA (117.1ip/34er), 115 strikeouts, 19 walks and a 0.96 WHIP in 22 total Minor League games (21 starts)…Tied all pitchers in MiLB in wins (five) and his 2.52 ERA ranked fifth in the International League from 8/17 through the end of the season.
2023
Went a combined 7-6 with a 3.53 ERA (127.1ip/50er) and 146 strikeouts in 26 starts between Bradenton and Greensboro…Finished tied for the organizational lead in strikeouts while also ranking second among Pirates farmhands in ERA…Began the season with Bradenton…Struck out seven batters in 5.0 scoreless innings while earning the win in his professional debut on 4/7 vs. Clearwater…Won each of his first four decisions before being charged with his first career loss (5.1ip/2er) on 5/19 at Clearwater…Ranked fourth among all Florida State League pitchers with a 2.77 ERA at the time he was promoted from Bradenton to Greensboro on 6/1…Recorded 106 strikeouts with Greensboro beginning on 6/1, which were tied for the most among all pitchers at the High-A level through the remainder of the season...Allowed three runs in 2.1 innings in his High-A debut on 6/2 at Winston-Salem…Allowed two hits while striking out eight batters in 7.0 scoreless innings on 6/8 vs. Wilmington…Was named the South Atlantic League Pitcher of the Week for the week of 6/5-11…Struck out 11 batters in 7.0 innings while allowing one run on 8/1 vs. Asheville.

Jared Keith Jones...Wife’s name is Rylie...Is a 2020 graduate of La Mirada (Calif.) High School...Had a 0.82 ERA and 28 strikeouts over 17.0 innings as a senior...Was also recognized as the 2019 Perfect Game/Rawlings Two-Way Player of the Year for the state of California...Was committed to pitch at the University of Texas at Austin...Was tabbed by both Baseball America (No. 41) and MLB Pipeline (No. 55) as a top prospect in the 2020 Draft...His father, Keith, was selected by Arizona in the 1997 Draft and played two seasons with the organization...Was signed by Pirates scout Brian Tracy.
2025
Was placed on the 15-day injured list on 3/27 (retro to 3/24)...Was transferred to the 60-day injured list on 3/31...Underwent surgery to repair his right UCL on 5/21 (surgery was performed by Dr. Keith Meister in Dallas, Texas).
2024
Made the Opening Day roster and made his Major League debut on 3/30 at Miami; started and won his first big league game (5.2ip/3er)...Struck out 10 batters in his debut; the most by a Pirates pitcher since Tim Wakefield on July 31, 1992, and one shy of the club record set by Nick Maddox on Sept. 13, 1907...Also became the 31st pitcher (19th in the National League) since 1900 to record 10 or more strikeouts in his MLB debut; the last to do it was Freddy Peralta of the Brewers on May 13, 2018...Started the Home Opener on 4/4 vs. Baltimore and suffered his first loss (6.0ip/2er)...Struck out at least seven batters in each of his first five starts, matching the Major League record for most such games to start a career and the second Pirate to do so, joining Pittsburgh’s Jose DeLeon (July 23-Aug. 10, 1983), Washington’s Stephen Strasburg (June 8-28, 2010) and New York’s Masahiro Tanaka (April 4-27, 2014)...Did not walk a batter in 21.1 consecutive innings from 4/5-22; the fifth-longest streak by a Major League pitcher within their first five career games since 1971...Won his second decision on 4/22 vs. Milwaukee (6.0ip/1er)...Induced 25 swing-and-misses on 4/22, matching the most by a Pirates pitcher in a single game since pitch data started being tracked in 2008; A.J. Burnett (Sept. 21, 2013) and Francisco Liriano (Sept. 11, 2014) are the others to accomplish this feat...Tossed 5.0+ innings and allowed three or fewer runs in each of his five career games, matching the most by a Pirates pitcher to start their career; joining Nick Maddox (1907), Cy Blanton (1934-35), Pascual Perez (1980- 81) and Gerrit Cole (2013)...Pitched 7.0 scoreless innings, allowing only one baserunner (was perfect thru 5.0ip) while striking out 10 batters and walking none on 5/4 vs. Colorado (no-decision)...His 10 strikeouts on 5/4 and 3/30 matched him with Jose DeLeon (1983) as the only two Pirates to whiff 10 or more batters twice in their first seven MLB starts...It also marked the fourth time Jones recorded seven or more strikeouts without a walk; the most ever by a MLB pitcher in the first seven starts of his career...Became the first Pirates pitcher to record an outing of 7.0+ scoreless innings, one or fewer hits, 10 strikeouts and zero walks on 5/4...Pitched 5.0- plus innings and allowed three or fewer earned runs in each of his first 10 career starts, matching Gerrit Cole’s club mark set in 2013; he became the ninth player since 1900 to put up those numbers in each of his first 10 career games and the first since Masahiro Tanaka in 2014...Tossed 6.0 scoreless innings and won a 1-0 decision over Tyler Glasnow and the Dodgers at PNC Park on 6/4...Was placed on the 15-day injured list on 7/4 with a right lat strain...Set the club record for most strikeouts by a rookie prior to the All-Star break with 98 (previous mark was 79 by Cy Blanton in 1935)... Began a rehab assignment with Indianapolis on 8/8 at Nashville...Was reinstated from I.L. on 8/27...Struck out nine batters and retired the final 16 batters he faced while winning his last game on 9/8 vs. Washington...Went 4-3 with a 2.87 ERA (69.0ip/22er) in 12 starts at PNC Park and 2-5 with a 5.81 ERA (52.2ip/34er) in 10 starts on the road.
2023
Entered the season rated as the organization’s No. 11 prospect according to Baseball America…Attended big league camp as a non-roster invitee…Finished tied for the organizational lead in strikeouts (146) along with Thomas Harrington (his 3.85 ERA was also the third-lowest among Pirates farmhands with at least 90.0 innings pitched)...Began the year with Double-A Altoona, where he earned the team’s Pitcher of the Year Award after allowing two runs or fewer in each of his 10 starts…Was placed on the seven-day injured list on 4/23 (retro to 4/21) due to lower back spasms…Was reinstated from the injured list on 5/10… Pitched 6.0 no-hit innings before giving up a solo home run in the seventh and losing a 2-0 decision on 6/8 at Richmond...Was promoted to Indianapolis on 6/20 and made his Triple-A debut that night vs. Columbus...Finished the month of July tied for the second-most strikeouts (32) in the International League… Struck out a season-high 10 batters while allowing one run in 6.0ip on 8/27 vs. Iowa (his third career double-digit strikeout game)...Recorded a 1.02 ERA (17.2ip/2er) in his final three starts with Indianapolis...Led all pitchers at the Triple-A level with 90 strikeouts from 7/1 through the end of the season.
2022
Spent the entire season with High-A Greensboro…Led the South Atlantic League in starts while also finishing second in innings pitched, fourth in batting average against (.246), sixth in WHIP and seventh in ERA…Led all Pirates farmhands in strikeouts, which were the most by a Pirates Minor Leaguer since Luis Escobar recorded 168 during the 2017 season…Struck out seven batters in 3.1 innings while allowing one run in his season debut on 4/12 at Winston-Salem…Scattered two hits in 5.0 scoreless innings in his next outing while also striking out eight batters to earn his first win on 4/17 at Winston-Salem…Finished the month of April with 26 strikeouts in 16.0 innings, tied for the fourth-most punchouts in the South Atlantic League…Allowed a combined nine runs, including four home runs, in 7.2 innings in his last two starts in April…Earned the win in his first outing of May before losing three of his next four starts during the month… Recorded the second double-digit strikeout game of his career with 10 punchouts on 5/28 at Asheville…Went 0-4 in 10 starts from 5/11 to 7/2 before winning on 7/8…Went 3-0 in his final four starts during the month of July…Recorded a 2.49 ERA (21.2ip/6er) in his final five starts.

Isaac Gerald Mattson
Isaac Gerald Mattson...Wife’s name is Devin...Has a son...Is a 2014 graduate of Harbor Creek (Pa.) High School...Where he had a 0.67 ERA and a .531 average as a senior...Attended the University of Pittsburgh (2015-17)...Was signed by Angels scout Jared Barnes.
2025
Pitched in three spring games as a non-roster invitee...Began the season with Indianapolis, where he went 2-0 with four saves, a 2.50 ERA (18.0 IP/5 ER), a .182 batting average against and a 0.94 WHIP in his first 16 appearances from 4/1-5/17 (G1)...Was selected by Pittsburgh on 5/20 when Colin Holderman was placed on the 15-day injured list...Allowed one run (surrendered a solo home run to Christian Yelich) and struck out two batters over 1.0 inning of work in his season debut on 5/22 vs. Milwaukee...Pitched in two more games (2.0 IP) from 5/23-25 vs. the Brewers before being optioned back to Indianapolis on 5/26...Made three more appearances (3.0 IP/1 ER) from 5/29-6/4 before being recalled by the Pirates on 6/7...Earned his first Major League win that afternoon vs. Philadelphia after stranding a runner at third base with no outs in a 1-1 game in the top of the seventh inning (Henry Davis hit a game-winning, solo home run in the bottom of that inning)...Posted a 1.54 ERA (11.2 IP/2 ER), 12 strikeouts and a .128 batting average against in eight June outings...Was scored upon in only one of his 13 appearances from 5/23-7/8 (he allowed two runs in 0.2 IP on 6/19 [G2] at Detroit)...Recorded a 1.54 ERA (11.2 IP/2 ER), 11 strikeouts and a .175 batting average against in 12 August appearances...His .203 batting average against from 5/22 (season debut) through the end of the season was the third-lowest among all Major League rookie relief pitchers (minimum 170 at-bats), trailing only St. Louis’ Matt Svanson (.163) and Chicago (AL)’s Mike Vasil (.185)...His 2.45 ERA from 5/22 through the end of the season ranked fourth among all Major League rookie relievers (minimum 45.0 IP), behind St. Louis’ Riley O’Brien (1.59), Vasil (1.75) and Svanson (1.84)...His .203 batting average against was also the fifth-lowest by a Pittsburgh rookie reliever with at least 170 at-bats, trailing only Luke Walker (.163) in 1968, David Bednar (.185) in 2021, Justin Wilson (.192) in 2013 and Roy Sanders (.198) in 1918.
2024
Went 7-2 with four saves, a 3.17 ERA (71.0ip/29r/25er) and 89 strikeouts in 37 Minor League games (three starts) between Altoona and Indianapolis...Was named Indy’s’ Pitcher-of-the-Year after going 5-1 with a 3.15 ERA (60ip/21er) and 76 strikeouts in 29 games (three starts)…Began the season with Altoona, where he went 2-1 with a save and a 3.27 ERA (11ip/4er) in eight relief appearances thru 5/4...Picked up wins in each of his first two appearances on 4/5 at Akron and 4/9 vs. Harrisburg...Earned his lone save with Altoona on 4/18 at Bowie...Suffered a blown save in the eighth inning and gave up a walk-off home run while suffering his lone Double-A loss on 5/1 at Harrisburg...Was promoted to Indianapolis on 5/7...Suffered his only loss with Indy while making his first outing with the team on 5/10 at Louisville (3ip/1er)…Made his first start on 5/18 vs. Toledo and was charged with one unearned run in 2ip...Gave up two runs in 2.2 innings of work while picking up his first save with Indianapolis on 5/23 at Iowa...Pitched a season-high four innings (0r) and picked up his first win with Indy on 6/15 at Jacksonville...Made his third and final start on 6/30 at Rochester...Picked up wins in back-to-back outings on 7/29 at Omaha (2ip/0r) and 7/24 at Iowa (2ip/0r)…Went 3-0 with a 2.13 ERA (12.2ip/3er) and 16 strikeouts in six appearances during the month of July...Won each of his last five decisions with Indianapolis and posted a 1.83 ERA (34.1ip/7er) in his final 18 appearances, dating back to 7/6... Had contract selected by Pittsburgh on 9/19...Made his debut with the Pirates on 9/20 at Cincinnati and retired all six batters he faced...Surrendered just one hit in his three big league games (17AB) for a .059 opponents batting average.
2023
Began season pitching with South Maryland in the independent Atlantic League...Went 1-1 with a 3.32 ERA (19.0ip/7er) and three saves in 18 appearances...Signed a Minor League deal with Minnesota on 6/22 and was assigned to Double-A Wichita...Made his lone start on 8/9 and tossed 2.1 scoreless innings...Was charged with just one earned run in his final seven games (13.1ip)
2022
Made 19 appearances with Norfolk (Orioles’ AAA)…Won his lone game on 6/9 at Nashville (Game 1)…Was released by Baltimore on 7/18...Signed with the Washington Wild Things on 8/6 and made 12 appearances.
2021
Recalled from Triple-A Norfolk on 5/3 and made his Major League debut on 5/7 vs. BOS (0.2 IP, H, ER, BB)…Threw a career-high-tying 1.1 scoreless innings on 7/3 at LAA, retiring four of his five batters faced; struck out David Fletcher for his first-career strikeout...Struck out a career-high two batters through 1.0 inning of work on 8/7 vs. TB...Went 0-2 with a 6.23 ERA (12 ER/17.1 IP) in 18 relief appearances for Triple-A Norfolk...Appeared in five games during Spring Training, going 0-1 with a 5.79 ERA (3 ER/4.2 IP), three walks, and three strikeouts.
2020
Participated in the Orioles Alternate Training Site at Double-A Bowie...Added to the 40-man roster on November 20, 2020
2019
Split the season between the Angels Class A-Advanced (Inland Empire) affiliate, Double-A (Mobile) affiliate, and Triple-A (Salt Lake) affiliate, making a combined 37 appearances and posting a 2.33 ERA (19 ER/73.1 IP) with 110 strikeouts...Named a MiLB.com Organization All-Star...Following the season, pitched for the Mesa Solar Sox of the Arizona Fall League, appearing in seven games and posting a 1.69 ERA (2 ER/10.2 IP) while striking out 12...Named to the AFL Rising Stars game.
2018
Spent the season with Class-A Burlington and Class A-Advanced Inland Empire...Posted a 7-4 record with a 3.82 ERA (40 ER/94.1 IP) and 85 strikeouts in 25 games (11 starts)...Made 11 starts for Burlington, his only career professional starts.
2017
Named a Pioneer League Postseason All-Star...Spent the majority of his first professional season with Rookie-Level Orem; also made three appearances for the AZL Angels... Appeared in 20 combined games, posting a 1-0 record with a 1.44 ERA (5 ER/31.1 IP) and 47 strikeouts.
